text:
anya: Heads-up — infra gave a firm ETA slide this morning. We need to re-evaluate the MVP cutline and rollback guards for next month's release. Options: trim a couple features for MVP or accept a 2-week slip. Thoughts?

sam: ugh. which features are on the table?

anya: shortlist: 1) prompt-store telemetry export (low usage but adds infra pressure), 2) tenant-level SSO (enterprise auth work), 3) real-time embedding cache (embcache warm paths). Keeping embeddings cache helps latency & cost, so ideally we don't cut that.

maria: infra note — the main bottleneck is autoscaler rewrite + a kernel patch. Autoscaler merge is at least 9d if we want full QA. If we ship without it we risk sustained p95 spikes under load.

kevin: can we mitigate with conservative autoscale config and cap burst to dedicated GPUs? Might be ok for MVP but increases cost.

lina: from PM/UX: tenant SSO is a hard blocker for a couple sales deals, but maybe we can offer a pilot with manual onboarding (SAML admin assisted) as an interim.

anya: okay so practical options: A) Trim SSO for MVP + keep prompt telemetry + embcache; B) Trim prompt telemetry + keep SSO + embcache; C) Full ship but 2-week delay.

sam: prefer A if sales ok with manual pilot. It preserves user-perceived perf.

maria: A removes a few infra integration points and reduces QA surface. I can sign up for A if we also lock rollback & rate-limit policies.

kevin: proposed rollback guard (draft):
```
- If infra p95 latency > 1.2s for >5m AND error-rate increase > 0.8% => automatic fallback to canary model pool
- If tail latencies persist > 3m after fallback => emergency rollback of new autoscaler config
- Manual rollback window: first 48h after rollout with escalations to oncall-sre
```

anya: that looks reasonable. Add one more: a prompt quota throttle at 200rps to prevent noisy tenants from taking down the pool.

maria: agree. Also add tracing hooks to surface which route caused the spike — we need quick rollback criteria tied to route.

lina: for customer comms: we'll call this a "phased launch" and offer enrollment to a pilot SSO cohort. That keeps sales momentum.

kevin: ops asks: we need a canary traffic % plan. Recommend 5% -> 25% over 2hrs if p95 < 800ms and errors < 0.2%.

anya: decision check: team leaning A (trim tenant SSO from MVP, offer manual pilot), preserve embcache, keep prompt telemetry for now, but add quota throttle and strict rollback guards + canary ramp plan. Anyone strongly object?

sam: no objections from eng side.

maria: +1. I will scope the autoscaler safe-config and the rollback playbook.

lina: +1 for PM/UX, will draft customer pilot comms and demo script.

release-bot: Deploy window locked: target release date remains as planned. Canary schedule will be included in the release notes.

anya: action items:
- maria: autoscaler safe-config + rollback playbook (owner) — due EOD Fri
- kevin: canary ramp scripts + throttle implementation — due Tue
- lina: pilot comms + manual SSO onboarding plan — due Thu
- sam: update launch checklist and devdocs for telemetry toggle — due Wed

anya: thanks all — we'll reconvene Fri 11am if any blockers. :thumbsup:
